# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# Expectation for the doctor check `settings_valid` (DESIGN.md §7.1) against input/config.toml.
# How to read this file: tests/fixtures/doctor/node_layout/expect.json.
#
# THIS CHECK NEEDS NO NEW TEST SEAM, unlike the six unit-file checks: FMONERO_CONFIG_DIR is already a
# documented Paths override (§5b, Paths::discover), so the harness copies input/config.toml into a temp
# config dir and points FMONERO_CONFIG_DIR at it. Nothing in DESIGN.md has to change.
#
# THIS CASE: THE FILE PARSES AND FOUR KEYS ARE WRONG. input/config.toml's own header names each defect
# and why it matters; briefly: node.network "mainet" (bad enum), wallet.priority 7 (out of 0..4, and
# wallet2 would silently clamp it to the MOST EXPENSIVE tier), timeouts.node_sec 0 (a value that is
# either "no deadline", which §2d forbids outright, or "kill everything instantly"), and wallet.acount
# (an unknown key one edit from wallet.account -- so wallet.account is absent and must fall back to its
# default rather than making the document unloadable).
# ONE THING IN THAT FILE IS NOT A DEFECT AND MUST NOT BE REPORTED: node.url on port 18099. §2c's rule is
# scheme http plus a LITERAL loopback host, and says nothing about the port -- 18099 is the port §8's own
# gate commands give fmonero-mock. A detector that also pins the port makes every mock-backed AMBER row
# of §4b report a bad setting, which is the check-fails-on-a-correct-machine failure §7.1 warns about in
# three other rows.
# THE PRODUCER OF THE LIST IS Settings::invalid_keys() -> Vec<(String, String)> (§5b: "(key, why) for
# every key that is present but invalid -- the doctor's settings_valid"). So the detail is built from
# that, and `detail_contains` below names the four keys rather than any prose.
# NOTE THE ASYMMETRY §5b's DOC COMMENT CREATES: invalid_keys() reports keys that are PRESENT BUT
# INVALID. wallet.acount is present and is not a key at all, so whether it appears in that vector is a
# question §5b leaves open. Phase 0's reading is that it must -- §7.1's condition is "config.toml parses
# AND EVERY KEY IS IN THE §4 TABLE", which an unknown key violates, and a silently ignored unknown key
# is how a user's intended setting has no effect with no diagnostic. The Phase 2 doctor agent owns the
# final call and should record it.
# status `warn`, severity `warn`, class A, `fixable` true -- all four from §7.1's row.
# THE FIXER REWRITES ONLY THE INVALID KEYS to their defaults and keeps the rest (§7.1: "rewrite the
# invalid key to its default"), through WriteFile{config_file(), Settings::to_toml_bytes(&repaired),
# 0o600} (§7.1's Action list). It must NOT call Settings::save, which writes the file itself and bypasses
# the verbatim backup, the sha256 pair and actions.jsonl -- and therefore `doctor undo`.
# ROUND TRIP: this case is the natural input for the Phase 2 class-A gate --
# corrupt -> --fix -> assert -> `doctor undo latest` -> byte-compare against input/config.toml.
